references.text: Just before Luke 23:1, the Council (Sanhedrin) has interrogated Jesus and found him guilty of blasphemy. The whole assembly (ἅπαν τὸ πλῆθος αὐτῶν) rises to take him further to Pilate. See [ref:Luk 22:66-71|Luke 22:66-71].

Matthew's parallel account of the Jewish leaders binding Jesus and taking him to the governor Pilate. The expression "the whole Council" corresponds with Luke's "the whole assembly". See [ref:Matt 27:1-2|Matthew 27:1-2].
Mark's parallel account of the chief priests, the elders, the scribes and the whole Council holding a consultation, binding Jesus and handing him over to Pilate. See [ref:Mark 15:1|Mark 15:1].
John's parallel account of them taking Jesus from Caiaphas to the governor's palace (the praetorium) to bring him before Pilate. See [ref:Joh 18:28|John 18:28].
Peter later refers to this event and accuses the people of having denied Jesus "before Pilate" – a direct reference to their handing him over to the Roman authority. See [ref:Apg 3:13|Acts 3:13].

In the early church's prayer, it is mentioned that "Herod and Pontius Pilate" gathered against Jesus, which reflects the sequence of events where Jesus was brought before Pilate. See [ref:Apg 4:27|Acts 4:27].

Paul refers in his speech at Antioch to how the inhabitants of Jerusalem and their rulers found no ground for death in Jesus, yet still asked Pilate to have him executed. This reflects the handing over to Pilate. See [ref:Apg 13:28|Acts 13:28].
Paul mentions Christ Jesus as having made the good confession "before Pontius Pilate", which presupposes the event where Jesus was brought before Pilate. See [ref:1 Tim 6:13|1 Timothy 6:13].
